Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
1212 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Mostly sunny, dry and above seasonable temps through Saturday.

2) Potential for a coastal low pressure to affect the area late
Sunday into early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Strong surface high pressure to dominate the weather over much 
of the eastern half of the country through the end of the week 
and into the beginning of the weekend. A moderating airmass
under ridging will have high temperatures running several
degrees above normal (upper 50s to middle 60s) thru Saturday.

Given the clear and dry conditions under a weak pressure 
gradient, low temperatures each night through Friday night, and
potentially Saturday Night, will be largely determined by radiational
cooling. Overall expect a gradual moderation in overnight lows 
to a few-several degrees above seasonable for late week into 
the weekend, particularly for urban and immediate coastal areas.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
A coastal low appears likely to develop off the Southeast coast
this weekend. The sys is then progged to lift to the NE as an 
upr trof approaches. There remains significant uncertainty 
regarding the exact track and timing of the low into next week, 
but the potential remains for the area to receive 1-2 inches of 
rain with locally higher amounts from late Sunday into the 
beginning of next week. 

The 00Z GFS and 00Z AI-GFS are close enough to the area, 
bringing rain and wind up the coast late Sun and persisting 
thru Mon. The ECMWF is slower and farther south and east with
the low track, being less impactful. There is still some 
uncertainty at this juncture in time. 

The NBM consensus brings roughly a 30-60 percent chance of rain
to the area, and these numbers were accepted considering the
uncertainty this far out. The modeling does suggest a sharp
gradient on the wrn edge of the pcpn field. 

The modeling also indicates the potential for the low to drop
into the 980s close to the area. This would produce some gusty
winds for at least some of the cwa. Winds will be proportional 
to the depth of the low, so in this case would estimate peak 
gusts in the 30-40mph range based on the 00Z GFS/AI-GFS. There 
are some hints of a deeper low, with the ECMWF in the 960s S of 
the benchmark after traversing the Gulf Stream. A track that far
E however would have limited impacts despite the intensity.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
High pressure in control through the TAF period. VFR prevails. 

Wind speeds 5-8 kt at most terminals this afternoon, then fall to 
around or under 5 kt later tonight, with calm winds for most 
outlying terminals. The prevailing wind direction will be generally
from the NW to WSW throughout the TAF period. Wind speeds will be 
generally 3 to 8 kt for late morning and afternoon Thursday.      

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind directions could be off by 20-30 degrees from TAF at 
times this afternoon.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Thursday through Monday... 

Thursday: VFR, light NW to WSW winds.

Friday-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Monday: MVFR or lower likely early in RA, improvement possible PM.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Sub SCA conditions expected on all waters through Sunday 
morning as high pressure keeps a weak pressure gradient over 
the area. Winds will mostly be from the NW-W at less than 15kt 
with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 to 3 ft. 

Next chance for SCA conditions will be later Sunday into Monday,
dependent on track and intensity of a coastal low pressure
developing off the SE US coast.
